headline: Evaluation design sets what performance claims mean in biological prediction
label: Standardized Benchmarking Of Predictive Models
summary: Recent preprints audit leakage, saliency validity and statistical inference, pressing for standardized, reportable evaluation in biological models.
synthesis: The common thread is that evaluation design determines what performance claims mean in biological prediction. A leakage audit of cancer drug response prediction reports that pre-CV feature screening inflates error estimates, with 23 of 32 audited published methods showing leakage. A counterfactual perturbation protocol validates saliency maps in siRNA efficacy prediction and exposes cross-dataset failure modes. On the statistical side, SIR applies nonparametric 2D isotonic-regression synergy scoring with wild-bootstrap p-values to drug combination matrices, and GRAPE regresses pairwise genetic interaction effects in pooled combinatorial CRISPR screens, validated with the Synulator simulation pipeline. What is new is treating validation, partitioning and inference as standardized, reportable components rather than incidental choices. These items do not share a single method; they share a concern with reproducible, comparable assessment.
